resource.name: Environment_NYC
resource.description: Street tree records from the 2015 TreesCount! census run by NYC Parks and partners. Fields include species, diameter, and perceived health. Collection ran from May 2015 to October 2016 and covers trees along city streets under Parks jurisdiction; the dataset is a point-in-time snapshot. The census data supports the agency's forestry inventory and management.
columns_description: Indicates the user's perception of tree health.
Unique identification number for each tree point.
Diameter of the tree, measured at approximately 54" / 137cm above the ground. Data was collected for both living and dead trees; for stumps, use stump_diam
Indicates whether the tree is alive, standing dead, or a stump.
Indicates the presence of a root problem caused by paving stones in tree bed
The species of the tree, which can influence its health due to species-specific resilience to urban conditions.
The borough in which the tree is located, as environmental conditions and urban stressors can vary by borough.
An index representing the quality of the soil in the area, which can affect tree health.
The average precipitation in the area where the tree is located, as water availability affects tree health.
The average temperature in the area, as extreme temperatures can stress trees.
The level of pollution in the area, as pollution can negatively impact tree health.
The distance of the tree from major roads, as proximity to traffic can influence tree health.
The frequency of maintenance activities such as pruning and watering, which can affect tree health.
A trend indicator of the tree's health over previous assessments, if available.
The percentage of canopy cover in the area, which can influence microclimate and tree health.
